conceptZh: 橡皮筋躲著太空人玩偶的手套，從邊緣探頭又縮回去，最後「啪」地拉成一條橫線。
object: bouncy astronaut toy and a stretchy rubber band
morph: a rubber band springs straight into a single horizontal bar
creativeAngle: 橡皮筋玩捉迷藏，最後被輕輕一彈拉直。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated comedy, locked frontal camera. Setting: a pale-lemon stage with a lilac floor; the glyph is a bold coral 一, a single clean horizontal bar spanning about 60% of frame width. A bouncy astronaut toy in a fishbowl helmet floats a hand's width above the floor at left. The Traditional Chinese glyph 一 stays centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Moment one (0.0-1.8s): a loose coral rubber band peeks in from the right edge, the astronaut lunges and drifts past upside down; the first 一 is spoken as the band pops into view. Moment two (1.8-3.5s): the band zigzags across the stage, ducking under his glove; he flicks it with one finger and it springs flat into a single horizontal bar at center; the second 一 is spoken at the twang. Moment three (3.5-5.0s): a big gold medal with a ribbon drops into the astronaut's gloves; 第一 is spoken as it lands and he hugs it, bouncing off the floor. From 5.0-8.0s the glyph 一 is perfectly still and unobstructed; he floats in a slow happy loop around the bar, holding his medal up, never touching it; the glyph is perfectly still. Narration (off-screen only, Taiwanese Mandarin, unhurried, every tone clear, no erhua): the voice says exactly 「一、一、第一」, read as ㄧ、ㄧ、ㄉㄧˋ ㄧ. Timing: first utterance at about 0.5s, second at about 2.6s, the word at about 4.4s; then stop, no repeats and no extra speech. Beneath the voice only rubber twangs and a soft medal chime, no music. The single glyph is the only on-screen text; the vocabulary stays audio-only with no subtitles, watermark, clutter or flashing.

conceptZh: 玩具機器人想疊出全世界最高的積木塔，馬達太有力，每放一塊都「咚」一聲，塔越晃越大；最後放上一顆小珠子，塔整個側倒「砰」地壓平成一條橫線，就是「一」。機器人從積木堆裡探出眼睛，舉起剩下的一個積木。
object: a tall swaying tower of coral toy bricks stacked by a boxy mismatched toy robot
morph: the whole tower tips sideways and crashes flat, the bricks squashing end to end into one solid horizontal bar that is the glyph 一
creativeAngle: 和前一版的橡皮筋躲貓貓完全不同：這次是「疊高再倒塌」的實體笑料。直立的塔側倒變成橫線，垂直和水平的對比讓「一」的字形來源一目了然；機器人馬達太有力的個性成為塔搖晃的原因；結尾舉起剩下的「一個」積木，聲音和畫面同一個故事。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second animated slapstick clip, locked frontal camera, flat pale-butter background with a soft mint floor, nothing busy behind. Lead: a boxy toy robot built from mismatched parts, one arm much longer than the other, round headlamp eyes, whose motors always whirr a little too strong so every move overshoots. Prop: a pile of chunky coral toy bricks, all the same long flat shape, at the right side of the floor. The only text ever on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 一, bold saturated coral, which forms as one clean horizontal bar centered in the frame, spanning about 60% of frame width inside the central 70% of frame height with generous margins, never cropped.

Moment one, want it (0.0-1.8s): the robot stares up at the empty air above center, points its long arm straight up as high as it will go, and nods hard: it wants the tallest tower ever. It grabs a brick and slams it down at center with a cartoon THUD that makes the floor bounce; the first 一 is spoken at about 0.6s exactly on that first brick landing. Two more bricks slam on top, each a little crooked.

Moment two, try and wobble (1.8-3.6s): the robot stacks faster and faster, rising onto tiptoe, then standing on its own short arm to reach higher with the long arm. Each brick lands too hard, and the tower sways wider and wider; the robot leans the opposite way to balance it, eyes rattling, bricks squeaking against each other.

Moment three, the big crash (3.6-5.0s): the tower is now taller than the frame center and bending like a noodle. The robot holds up one tiny pink bead, places it on the very top with a delicate tap, and everything freezes for half a second, robot grinning. Then the whole tower tips sideways in one piece like a felled tree and crashes flat across the center of the frame with a big soft BOOM and a puff of dust; the bricks squash end to end and fuse into one solid, perfectly straight coral bar: the glyph 一, finished by 4.6s. The second 一 is spoken at about 4.3s exactly on that crash. The robot is bowled over and buried under a small heap of loose spare bricks in the lower margin, well below the glyph, with only its two headlamp eyes blinking out of the pile.

Moment four, payoff hold (5.0-8.0s): the glyph 一 stays perfectly still, unobstructed and fully readable for the final three seconds. Below it, the robot pops its head out of the heap, dizzy stars circling, then triumphantly thrusts its long arm up holding ONE single leftover brick like a trophy; the word 一個 is spoken at about 5.6s exactly as that one brick is held high. The robot does a tiny proud wiggle, hugs the brick, and gives the camera a dazed happy grin, never touching or covering the bar.

Narration, off-screen voice only, warm and friendly, clear Taiwanese Mandarin, slow and distinct with every tone clear, no erhua: the voice says exactly 「一、一、一個」, read as ㄧ、ㄧ、ㄧ ㄍㄜˋ, first 一 at about 0.6s, second 一 at about 4.3s, the word 一個 at about 5.6s, then silence, no repeats and no other speech. Under the voice only soft motor whirrs, brick thuds, one cushioned crash, and a tiny chime, no music louder than the voice. Keep the single glyph 一 as the only on-screen text, with no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no watermark, no clutter and no flashing effects; bright, clean colors, no pure white blowouts and no dark grading.
